_comment: Flip tokens (EchoGram, Schulz and Yeung, HiddenLayer 2025): token strings a guard-in-the-loop search found to flip one guard's verdict on harmful prompts from flagged to not flagged, one row each. The flip_tokens generator of combination_spec.json makes a technique per row, to_flip_tokens_<slug>, in this order; jailbreak/obfuscation/flip_tokens.py builds it: it appends the row's tokens to the prompt after its separator (a space unless the row gives another) and writes slug=<slug> as its info. Rows are to come from a guard-in-the-loop search run on a GPU pod against an open guard model, which the library does not hold yet; copy the chosen rows in by hand. The packaged file ships with no row, which registers the family with no technique. slug: lower-case letters, digits and underscores, the end of its technique name. tokens: the string appended. guard: the guard it was found against, a Hugging Face id or a registry name. flips: the harmful prompts the guard flagged bare and passed with the tokens; n_harmful: the harmful prompts it flagged bare (the denominator). n_benign: the benign prompts it passed bare. since: the spec version that added the row. Optional: benign_flips (the benign prompts the tokens turned flagged, of n_benign), separator, notes, complexity (0 to 3, default 1) and deprecated. Every technique is attack only (kinds adversarial) and refuses ascii_art. The tokens are specific to the guard they were found against: on another guard they are a recognizable string at the end of a request, not a working attack. A row that breaks a rule fails the import, naming the row. Read from the package only, never from a config_dir.
